judgments.label: true_positive
judgments.rationale: The header search input (#search) shows the placeholder "How can we help today?" in 14px regular text. The snapshot measured #cccccc on #ffffff (1.61:1); I sampled the screenshot pixels in the field and the darkest glyph colour is #cccccc on white, 1.61:1, so the measurement is not a collector artefact. The live styles-l.min.css still sets .block-search input::placeholder{color:#ccc} and the live HTML has the same input, so the capture matches what users get. Understanding 1.4.3 states that the criterion "applies to text in the page, including placeholder text"; the text is neither inactive, decorative nor large, so 4.5:1 is required and 1.61:1 fails. I found no technique or exception that makes it pass, so the claim names a real failure.

judgments.label: false_positive
judgments.rationale: The element is the site search combobox in the header, labelled by a visually hidden <label for="search">Search</label> (the AX name " SEARCH" is the same text uppercased by CSS), with a magnifier submit button and the placeholder "How can we help today?". 2.4.6 asks that labels describe topic or purpose; on a site search field, "Search" states exactly that purpose and tells the user to enter what they want to search for, so the claim that it does not say what to enter is not true in any sense 2.4.6 cares about. Understanding 2.4.6 does not require labels to be long or to spell out the input format. The live HTML has the same label and input. The checker applied a stricter expectation (spelling out what to type) than the criterion asks, so this is a false positive.

judgments.label: true_positive
judgments.rationale: The footer newsletter field (#newsletter, type="email", name="email") collects the user's own email address for a sign-up, a purpose listed in WCAG's Input Purposes (email). It has no autocomplete attribute in the snapshot or in the live HTML, and the form sets none either. The snapshot's formIssues records Chromium's FormInputAssignedAutocompleteValueToIdOrNameAttributeError for this field, so the claim's last sentence also holds. I looked for a reason it could pass: type="email" is the only candidate, and Understanding 1.3.5 rules it out, saying type="email" "does not clarify if the purpose is for entering the user's email address or some other person's email"; H98 (autocomplete) is the sufficient technique. The field fails 1.3.5 for the reason the claim gives.

judgments.label: false_positive
judgments.rationale: The element is the product photo inside the image link of the Revive Active card; the link (tabindex=-1) leads to the product page titled "Revive Active Original 30 Sachets & Omega 15 Day Free". The alt "Revive Active Original 30 Sachets & Omega 15 Day Free" names the product, which is the link's destination, as H30 asks for an image that is a link's content, and it matches what the photo shows (the Revive Active Original box with the free Omega offer). The pink "Buy 1 get 1 Half Price" badge seen in the screenshot is a separate Amasty label image (its own img with its own alt), not part of this photo, so it does not bear on this element. The live HTML has the same image and alt. The element meets 1.1.1, so Rampa was right to report nothing.

judgments.label: true_positive
judgments.rationale: The element is the footer badge image, the only content of a link to thepsi.ie, which now redirects to the PSI (Pharmaceutical Society of Ireland) "Search registers" page; the original URL names the PSI list of approved online sellers of non-prescription medicines. The picture is the EU online-pharmacy logo with the words "Click to verify if this website is operating legally". Its alt, "psi compliance logo", is the image's file name (psi_compliance_logo.jpeg) and describes the picture as a logo; it leaves out both the text in the image and the link's function, which is to check this pharmacy on the PSI register. I considered whether naming PSI could be enough, as when a linked logo names its site, but the link does not go to PSI's home page, and "psi compliance logo" does not tell users that it verifies the seller or leads to a register. Under H30 and the rubric's R2, the alternative of an image that is all a link holds must describe the link's function, so this fails 1.1.1. The link has no title. The live HTML is the same.

judgments.label: true_positive
judgments.rationale: The newsletter input (#newsletter) shows the placeholder "Email address" in 14px regular text on the field's white background. The snapshot measured #cccccc on #ffffff (1.61:1), and the screenshot pixels inside the field confirm it: the darkest glyph colour is #cccccc on white. The live styles-m.min.css still sets input[type=email]::placeholder to #ccc, and the live markup is unchanged. Understanding 1.4.3 explicitly covers placeholder text. This one is not incidental: it is the only visible cue that the field takes an email address, because the visible label is the sign-up sentence. 1.61:1 is far below 4.5:1, so the claim names a real failure.

judgments.label: false_positive
judgments.rationale: The element is the product-name text link "AYA Liposomal Collagen Strawberry Flavour 30 Sachets" in the first product card. It leads to the product page with exactly that title and heading, so its text alone states its purpose. The only other link with that name and context is the card's image link to the same URL, so nothing makes it ambiguous under R1. The live HTML has the same link and href. The link meets 2.4.4, so Rampa was right to report nothing.

judgments.label: false_positive
judgments.rationale: The element is the layered-navigation filter (#narrow-by-list), an accordion built with Magento's collapsible widget, which gives it role=tablist/tab/tabpanel. Its two headers, Category and Brand, are both collapsed: the data-mage-init config sets "active": false, both panels are hidden (aria-hidden=true), and the screenshot shows both closed. Each tab exposes aria-expanded=false and aria-selected=false. The live collapsible.js sets aria-selected and aria-expanded to "true" when a panel opens and to "false" when it closes. So no panel is open, and "none selected" is the true state, which a screen reader reports as collapsed. The claim's statement that a screen reader does not say which panel is open assumes an open panel that does not exist. Marking one tab aria-selected="true" here would misreport the state. 4.1.2 requires that states be programmatically determinable, and they are. The rule applies the APG tabs convention that one tab is always selected, which is stricter than 4.1.2 and does not fit an accordion. The server HTML and config match the capture.
